newsitem.title: USA: Maine Yankee extends 910 MW nuke outage.
newsitem.headline: Maine Yankee extends 910 MW nuke outage.

text.p: Maine Yankee Atomic Power Co Friday said it extended the current shutdown of its 910 megawatt (MW) nuclear power station to mid-February for inspection of the plant's 217 fuel rod assemblies.
"Maine Yankee estimates the entire project can be completed in mid-February," it said in a statement.

Daily monitoring showed there may be pinhole-sized openings in four to six of Maine Yankee's 38,000 fuel rods that house uranium fuel pellets. These holes permit water to enter and exit the pressurized metal rods, the company said.
This condition, which is permitted within Nuclear Regulatory Commission limits, has caused a slight increase in iodine levels in the reactor coolant water, it said.
If pinholes are detected, the defective rods will be replaced, Maine Yankee said.

Although the rise in iodine levels is slight, Maine Yankee decided to take advantage of the current outage and inspect the assemblies now rather than wait until the next refueling outage, scheduled for this autumn, it said.
The Maine Yankee facility was taken off line December 6 to review cable separation issues, and this week went from hot to cold shutdown to test circuitry used to activate diesel generators.

Maine Yankee is 38 percent owned by Central Maine Power Co, 20 percent each by New England Electric System and Northeast Utilities, seven percent by Bangor Hydro, five percent by Maine Public Service Co and 10 percent by other New England utilities.
